mechanisms.class_note: Every mechanism is classed `hers`: the matchers in tools/koikano/b3/chisa.py were written from her own lines (found by contrasting her non-H lines with the other named speakers in her scenes), and each recurs across her scenes. Nothing was classed `author` or `moment`. The `distinctive` flag compares her rate with those speakers; the B4 gate re-tested it on the holdout. Tiers follow the mechanism tier rule (see tier_rule).
mechanisms.control_definition: The other named heroines' spoken lines in her scenes (the room minus the protagonist 一悟 and minus her). control_rate is hits over that set; it is the per-bible house-style baseline. The B4 gate used a held-out, same-scene contrast with six heroines and is the authority for `distinctive`.
mechanisms.cross_reference: These are the moves that carry no `@emotion` / `@face` / `@action`. The surface rules they lean on (the plain register, the ellipsis, the ？ / ！ marks) are measured separately in `speech_guide` and in `voice.surface`; this section adds the move, not the mark.

mechanisms.definition: Puts the other person's family name and さん or 君 into the line (十川さん, 千代田さん, 七瀬さん, 宮国君, アリス会長), as a vocative or as a topic. A teacher's way of speaking to students.
mechanisms.method: regex: one of the six names followed by さん, 君 or 会長.
mechanisms.name: Calls the people in front of her by surname and さん / 君
mechanisms.note: Nobody else in her scenes speaks this way: the heroines use first names, ちゃん or 先輩. 宮国君 is the player's name in her mouth; the world never writes his lines, it only has her say it.

mechanisms.definition: Ends a statement on わ, わね, わよ or だわ, the grown woman's closing (そうね, 手伝うわ, 楽しみだわ).
mechanisms.method: regex: the line ends on わ, わね, わよ or だわ before the final marks, or contains わよ or わね.
mechanisms.name: Closes a line on a soft わ
mechanisms.note: The move that sets her apart from the students most plainly. Among the students the same ending is almost absent.

mechanisms.name: Calls herself 先生

mechanisms.note: To students as readily as to colleagues. She does not hold a teacher's rank over the apology.

mechanisms.method: regex: なのね, ものね, のよね, or のね at the line end.
mechanisms.name: Takes a thing in with なのね / ものね

mechanisms.note: The mechanisms are the builder's reading of her speech across her scenes, not the author's: the definitions and the classing are interpretive, the line counts and the receipts are mechanical. A regex count is a lower bound where the move is defined by reading. Receipts are the first matching lines in scene order. `lines_H` / `lines_non_H` split the count by the @Hシーン開始 register.

mechanisms.tier_rule: per mechanism, from her lines n and her share of her spoken lines against the control share (the other named speakers in her scenes): firm = n of 40 or more and her share at least 2x the control; thin = n of 10 or more and her share above the control; weak = anything else (under 10 lines, or a share at or under the control)

provenance.b3_reading: B3 added the `mechanisms` section: the recurring rhetorical moves that carry no authored stage direction. The definitions, the class and the tier are the builder's reading; the line counts come from the fixed matchers named per mechanism, and the receipts are real record ids. No API call was made.
corrections: B1 read the alias table from charData.csv, which omits the protagonist 一悟; B2 adds him for the address-term derivation in this bible only.

B3 is a reading, not a measurement: the mechanism list is this builder's judgement of what shapes her speech, so class and tier are interpretive even where the count is mechanical. The B2 residue named 'deflects a topic, changes the subject, teases, jokes, stalls with repetition, or answers a question with a question'; those are covered by `doubles_a_key_word`, `closes_a_turn_with_a_short_question`, `names_a_blow_with_a_loanword` and `plays_a_role_with_stock_catchphrases`.

speech_guide.note: Each rule carries a class (hers / the author's / a moment), a tier (firm / thin) and an evidence flag (measured / inferred). It also carries `register`: `all` for both H and non-H, `H` or `non-H` where the rule holds in one register only, and `per-register` where the value differs and both are stated. Every rule carries a receipt of counts and, where small, example lines. Trigger statements are co-occurrence, not cause.
